<image_1> In the transition-state structure shown in the image, calculate the total number of bonds in the structure, including single, double, and triple bonds but excluding those involving hydrogen.

Note: Disregard arrows. Consider all components present in the transition-state structure shown in the image.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The structure shows a benzene ring with an O⁻ substituent attached to the ring, a CHCl group attached to the ring, and another chlorine atom above/near the CHCl carbon as part of the transition-state depiction. Curved arrows are also drawn, but they are not bonds. Reasoning: Count only non-hydrogen bonds and disregard arrows. The benzene ring contributes 6 C-C bonds around the ring. The ring-to-O bond contributes 1. The ring-to-CHCl carbon bond contributes 1. The C-Cl bond represented in the CHCl label contributes 1, while the C-H bond is excluded. The additional C-Cl bond to the separate chlorine in the transition-state structure contributes 1. Total = 6 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 10.

method.method_draft: First describe the image contents, then count non-H bonds directly. Count the six C-C bonds around the benzene ring. Add the C-O bond from the ring to the O⁻ substituent. Add the C-C bond from the ring to the carbon labeled CHCl. Add the C-Cl bond represented by the Cl in the CHCl label. Add the additional C-Cl bond to the separate chlorine above in the transition state. Ignore all curved arrows and do not count the C-H bond in CHCl. The total is 6 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 10.

method.method_draft: Group the drawing into components. The benzene/phenyl core contributes 6 non-H ring bonds. The phenoxide substituent contributes 1 non-H bond, the aryl C-O bond. The side-chain transition-state carbon contributes 3 non-H bonds: one to the aryl ring, one to the chlorine written as part of CHCl, and one to the separate chlorine above. Do not count the C-H bond in CHCl and ignore all arrows. Summing by components gives 6 + 1 + 3 = 10.
